items.prompt: An operations team rebuilds an index for 40,000 equipment procedures containing headings and safety tables. During rollout, citations must never combine clauses from two revisions. Which indexing design should be selected?
constraints: Chunks must preserve section and table meaning.
Document and revision identity must remain coherent while the replacement index is built and switched.

options.text: Split procedures into equal windows, update vectors in place, and allow a newer matching chunk to outrank an older one during the rebuild.
Append the replacement chunks to the active index without revision filters and ask generation to reconcile any clauses that cite different versions.
Chunk by meaningful sections and intact tables with immutable document, revision, and section IDs; build and evaluate separately, switch atomically, then retire the old revision.
Index each entire procedure as one vector so tables remain together, accepting poor section precision and relying on document-level citations.

feedback.Reason: Section and table boundaries preserve meaning, while immutable revision identifiers and an atomic switch prevent mixed-version evidence during rollout.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Structure-aware chunks retain local headings, units, and table context; a versioned index lifecycle lets evaluation occur before the new corpus becomes authoritative.
Details.scenarioApplication: Tag every chunk with document, revision, section, and table identity, evaluate retrieval and citations on the new build, then switch the active revision as one operation.
Details.errorCorrection: Treat chunk boundaries and index lifecycle as evidence integrity controls, not just vector tuning settings.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Smaller structured chunks and parallel index builds require more metadata and storage, but they avoid incoherent citations and support rollback.
Details.transfer: For versioned RAG corpora, preserve semantic units and revision identity, evaluate a replacement index separately, and switch authority atomically.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Equal windows can split headings and tables, and in-place updates allow old and new revisions to rank together without a coherent switch.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Appending without revision filters leaves incompatible evidence available and asks generation to enforce a lifecycle policy it cannot guarantee.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Whole-document vectors preserve tables but lose section-level retrieval precision and make a large procedure harder to address.

items.prompt: After an equipment-manual migration, retrieval finds the correct section, but answers misstate a torque value because a table row was indexed without its column heading and unit. What should be repaired first?
constraints: A numeric answer needs the table labels and units in its evidence chunk.
The retrieval location is correct; the source-to-chunk transformation is the suspected fault.

options.text: Rebuild the chunk with its table heading, column labels, units, nearby procedure context, and section ID, then reindex and evaluate numeric answers against the source.
Increase embedding size and top-K, leave the isolated table row unchanged, and let generation select a plausible unit from nearby retrieved engineering passages.
Place the full manual in every request so Claude can infer the missing heading and unit from surrounding pages instead of changing the index.
Accept a numeric unit when it falls within a familiar engineering range and send only unusually large deviations to a reviewer.

feedback.Reason: The correct section cannot compensate for lost table semantics. Restoring heading, labels, units, and context in the chunk addresses the observed transformation defect before changing ranking.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Contextualized structure gives retrieval and generation the relationships needed to interpret a numeric row; reindexing and source comparison test whether the repair restores accuracy.
Details.scenarioApplication: Include table and section identifiers in each chunk, run torque holdouts with units, and reject answers whose evidence span does not support the numeric value.
Details.errorCorrection: Repair the evidence representation when the source-to-chunk boundary loses semantics; do not mask it with broader retrieval or inference.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Richer chunks increase index size and may reduce granularity, so evaluate them on numeric recall, citation support, and retrieval cost.
Details.transfer: When RAG finds the right location but the answer is wrong, inspect chunk structure and contextual labels before changing embeddings or model behavior.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: More vectors and top-K do not restore the missing heading or unit and can increase distractors while encouraging an inferred value.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A full manual raises context cost and hides the evidence boundary; it is not a targeted repair for a lost table label.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Plausibility is not source support, and accepting inferred units can propagate a silent numeric error.

items.prompt: A laboratory has a stable authoritative corpus of 90,000 tokens used for broad questions by a small analyst group. It fits the selected context window, and the changing question can follow the source. Which first-release boundary is proportionate?
constraints: The full authoritative corpus fits the target context with room for the question and response.
The workload is small enough that retrieval complexity needs measured justification.

options.text: Build vectors and a reranker immediately so the changing question can select a smaller context, even though the full authoritative corpus currently fits.
Provide the structured full corpus, place the variable question after it, cache the stable prefix where useful, and introduce RAG only when growth or context limits are measured.
Build a vector index with coarse topic chunks and rerank every question to reduce prompt size, even though the full authoritative corpus currently fits with room for the query.
Create a small extractive summary of the corpus for each request and link analysts to full sections only when they dispute an answer.

feedback.Reason: The corpus fits and is required broadly, so a structured full-context path is simpler and more authoritative than an unneeded retrieval layer. RAG can be introduced when measured size, latency, or query needs require it.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Tagged full context preserves authority and can reuse a stable prefix; retrieval becomes a later boundary when the corpus no longer fits or selective evidence improves measured performance.
Details.scenarioApplication: Load the corpus with document boundaries, put the changing question after it, and monitor context and latency before adding chunking and ranking infrastructure.
Details.errorCorrection: Choose RAG for a measured information-shape or scale problem rather than assuming every knowledge base needs vectors.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Full context may consume more tokens than selective retrieval, but it reduces indexing and ranking failure modes while the corpus fits.
Details.transfer: Start with the simplest authoritative context design that fits the workload, then introduce retrieval when corpus growth or relevance evidence justifies it.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Immediate indexing and reranking add operational complexity without a demonstrated context or relevance problem.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A retrieval layer and coarse topic chunks add indexing and ranking failure modes before the corpus needs selective access; they do not improve the already fitting full-context path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: An extractive summary can omit authoritative detail needed for broad questions, and a citation added only after dispute is too late for the normal answer.

items.prompt: A regulatory corpus contains millions of tokens and many similar clauses. Initial retrieval returns broadly related passages, but the answer depends on local context and precise relevance. Which TWO pipeline choices improve evidence quality? Select TWO.
constraints: Similar clauses need local document and location context.
Candidate count and reranking must be evaluated against relevance, latency, and cost.

options.text: Send the entire corpus to Claude so every similar clause remains available for the answer.
Use one vector for each complete document and rely on the model to locate the controlling clause in generation.
Rely only on frequent-word filtering so lexical overlap determines the final candidate set.
Prepend concise document and location context to candidate chunks so local meaning survives retrieval.
Rerank a measured initial candidate set and tune top-K against relevance, latency, and cost on representative queries.

feedback.Reason: Local context disambiguates similar clauses, and reranking can improve precision after an initial recall stage when top-K is measured. Both decisions address the observed broad relevance without overflowing context.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Contextualized chunks carry document and location clues; a reranker scores the initial candidates and the evaluation set links top-K to answer relevance and resource use.
Details.scenarioApplication: Add section and jurisdiction context, rerank lexical/semantic candidates, and select a top-K that meets citation and latency floors on regulatory queries.
Details.errorCorrection: Improve candidate evidence and ranking separately; do not ask generation to recover document location or choose among an unbounded corpus.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reranking and context expansion add compute and tokens, so their value must be balanced with candidate quality and cost.
Details.transfer: For similar legal or policy passages, preserve local provenance in chunks and validate reranking and top-K against the actual answer task.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The corpus exceeds useful context and leaves evidence selection and source location implicit.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A document-level vector loses the local distinctions that determine the controlling clause and forces generation to search inside a broad unit.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Word frequency misses semantic paraphrases and cannot reliably resolve similar clauses or their local scope.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Without local document and location context, similar clauses remain difficult to distinguish after retrieval.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Without measured reranking and top-K, the pipeline cannot improve precision while controlling latency and cost.

items.prompt: A safety manual contains cross-references where an exception starts in one section and its scope continues into the next. Fixed 300-token chunks retrieve the rule but omit the exception on boundary cases. Which chunking change should be tested?
constraints: Boundary-case answers need adjacent exception context.
The index should retain retrieval granularity rather than making every chunk a full manual.

options.text: Keep fixed windows and ask Claude to infer an omitted exception from general safety knowledge when a boundary case is detected.
Make each chunk the complete manual so every cross-reference is present, accepting a large context and losing section-level retrieval precision.
Use section-aware chunks with controlled overlap or parent-context expansion, then compare boundary recall and citation completeness with fixed chunks while tracking index and prompt cost.
Increase top-K until both sections appear, without changing boundaries or testing whether the extra sections introduce unrelated rules.

feedback.Reason: The failure is a chunk boundary that separates an exception from its governing rule. Controlled overlap or parent expansion restores adjacent scope while preserving meaningful retrieval units and makes the trade-off measurable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Section-aware chunking can include the next section or parent context when a cross-reference is detected; evaluation checks whether the exception and citation arrive together.
Details.scenarioApplication: Build boundary-case queries, compare fixed and overlap variants, and retain section IDs and neighboring references in the evidence returned to Claude.
Details.errorCorrection: Repair the chunk boundary and context expansion before relying on model inference or unbounded candidate counts.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Overlap increases index and prompt cost and can introduce duplicate passages, so use the smallest measured expansion that restores exception recall.
Details.transfer: For manuals and policies with cross-references, test structure-aware chunks and controlled neighboring context against boundary-case evidence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: General knowledge cannot safely supply a missing safety exception and hides the evidence gap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Whole-manual chunks destroy retrieval granularity and inflate context for ordinary questions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: More candidates may add the next section but does not guarantee adjacency or prevent irrelevant clauses from crowding the answer.

items.prompt: A tenant uploads revision R3 and deletes R2 under a retention policy, but R2 embeddings remain searchable and answers cite the deleted clause. Which index lifecycle change is required?
constraints: Deleted revision content must not answer current queries.
Retrieval and citation tests must enforce tenant and active-revision state.

options.text: Mark R2 unavailable, remove or tombstone its vectors, filter retrieval to the tenant's active revisions, and run deletion and citation tests before exposing R3.
Leave R2 vectors searchable for recall and instruct Claude to prefer R3 when both revisions appear, treating deletion as a generation preference.
Append R3 vectors and rely on its higher embedding score to make deleted R2 unlikely to be returned by current queries.
Keep R2 in the same tenant index and add a prompt note that historical clauses must not be quoted in current answers.

feedback.Reason: Retention and revision state are index and retrieval responsibilities. Tombstoning or removing R2 and filtering active revisions prevents stale evidence from reaching generation; tests prove the deletion boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The index lifecycle marks vectors unavailable and the retriever applies tenant and revision filters before evidence is returned; the model is not asked to enforce deletion from mixed chunks.
Details.scenarioApplication: Process the R2 deletion event, verify no active query retrieves it, index R3 with its version, and test citations against current and historical modes separately.
Details.errorCorrection: Enforce content lifecycle and authority before generation rather than relying on ranking, recency, or prompt admonitions.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Deletion propagation and tombstone checks add operational complexity and may reduce recall, but they protect retention obligations and citation correctness.
Details.transfer: For mutable corpora, treat deletion and version filters as retrieval invariants and test them at ingestion, index, query, and citation boundaries.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Claude cannot reliably enforce deletion or revision policy when stale and current chunks are both available.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A score preference does not remove deleted content and can still return R2 when the query matches it better.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A prompt note is not an index authorization or retention control and leaves the deleted clause searchable.

items.prompt:
A laboratory corpus has grown to four million tokens, while analysts ask one section-specific question per request. A full-context request exceeds the selected model window, and source citations must identify the active revision and section.

Which retrieval design should replace the infeasible full-context request?
constraints: The corpus is four million tokens and exceeds the selected model window; each query targets one section.
Documents have stable revision and section metadata, and source citations must identify them.
A 500-question benchmark can measure section-aware chunks, reranking, citation recall, and latency.

options.text: Keep the full corpus in every request because broad context prevents retrieval misses.
Use active-revision section-aware RAG with bounded reranking and source IDs; switch only after recall and latency meet the floor.
Chunk the corpus once and retrieve by similarity without filtering active revisions or attaching source IDs.
Use a short keyword match and switch immediately, deferring citation and latency evaluation until after rollout.

feedback.Reason: The size and query evidence remove the full-context option while leaving a measurable retrieval design to evaluate.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: RAG is useful for retrieving relevant chunks, but it is not always needed when a knowledge base fits in context; prompt caching can help repeated full context. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The corpus no longer fits the context window and the query is targeted, so full-context prompting must reverse to an evaluated RAG pipeline.
Details.scenarioApplication: Index active revisions into section-aware chunks, retrieve and rerank a bounded candidate set, include source IDs in context, and switch only after citation recall and latency meet the service floor.
Details.errorCorrection: The corpus cannot fit and broad context would exceed both model and cost budgets; it cannot prevent omissions by being rejected before inference.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the active corpus later fits within the model window and broad questions dominate, re-evaluate full context with a stable prefix.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The corpus cannot fit and broad context would exceed both model and cost budgets; rejecting the request cannot prevent omissions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Unfiltered chunks can surface retired sections and cannot satisfy the required active-revision citations or benchmarked evidence boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A first-match shortcut does not establish recall, answer quality, or tail latency for section-specific questions before a production switch.

items.prompt:
A parts assistant must answer two linked facts: the exact current availability of SKU AX-4407 and the manual explanation for why the item is restricted. The structured inventory updates hourly; the manual corpus updates weekly and contains similar historical clauses.

How should the assistant combine the current inventory fact with the manual explanation?
constraints: The inventory API is authoritative for hourly quantity and tenant scope.
Manual retrieval can filter active revision sections, but historical clauses remain during rollout.
The answer must keep source identity visible and stop when the two sources disagree on a restriction.

options.text: Run one semantic search over manual and inventory text and let the highest-scoring paragraph provide both facts.
Use the manual corpus as the sole source for availability and restriction because it contains more explanatory context.
Query authoritative inventory for quantity, retrieve active manual evidence for explanation, label sources, and escalate conflicts.
Return the inventory quantity and choose the most recent-looking manual restriction without exposing a conflict state.

feedback.Reason: The integrated answer preserves source authority and freshness instead of asking one semantic index to answer incompatible facts.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Retrieval should match the query and source shape; a structured metric lookup is better served by the metrics source than by semantic narrative search. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The pipeline must route each information need to its source shape and keep structured freshness and manual revision filters separate before combining the answer.
Details.scenarioApplication: Query the authorized inventory API for the exact SKU and current quantity, retrieve only active manual sections for the explanation, label each evidence source, and abstain or escalate if the two sources disagree on the restriction.
Details.errorCorrection: Semantic similarity cannot guarantee current quantity or tenant scope, and a historical manual clause can outrank the hourly structured record.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the inventory API is unavailable, expose quantity as unavailable and provide the manual explanation separately; do not infer current availability from prose.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Semantic similarity cannot guarantee current quantity or tenant scope, and a historical manual clause can outrank the hourly structured record.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Manual prose cannot establish hourly inventory or tenant scope and may contain historical clauses; the structured API remains authoritative for quantity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Choosing prose without active-revision evidence hides a source disagreement; the assistant must label sources and abstain or escalate when restriction evidence conflicts.
